- If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- Model consistently overpredicts mid-term (15–30d) prices when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5%.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it; adjust forecast to align with recent trend direction.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting; forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 3–5 prices are rising, model often overestimates; apply smoothing or lagged correction.
